## Services: Complete Descriptions

### 1. Kitchen Remodeling

**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/services/kitchen-remodeling

Mile High Custom Remodels provides end-to-end kitchen renovations for Denver Metro
homeowners — from a simple cabinet refresh to a complete gut-and-rebuild with structural
changes.

#### What Is Included

- Initial design consultation and space planning
- Demolition and debris disposal
- Custom or semi-custom cabinetry design, fabrication coordination, and installation
- Countertop selection, fabrication, and installation (quartz, granite, marble, quartzite,
  laminate, butcher block)
- Kitchen island design and construction
- Backsplash tile design and installation (subway tile, mosaic, large-format, stone)
- Flooring installation (hardwood, luxury vinyl plank, porcelain tile, natural stone)
- Under-cabinet and recessed lighting; pendant installation
- New appliance delivery and installation (range, refrigerator, dishwasher, microwave,
  range hood, garbage disposal)
- Plumbing rough-in and fixture installation (kitchen sink, faucet, pot filler, dishwasher
  water line, refrigerator ice maker line)
- Electrical work (new circuits, GFCI outlets, USB outlets, range hood venting)
- Structural work as needed (wall removal, load-bearing beam installation, window additions)
- Painting, caulking, and trim installation
- All permit applications, inspection scheduling, and final sign-offs
- Dedicated project manager from design phase through final punch list

#### Pricing Tiers — Kitchen Remodeling (Denver Metro, 2026)

| Tier         | Scope                                                                      | Typical Cost     |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| Basic        | Stock or RTA cabinets, laminate countertops, new fixtures, cosmetic updates| $25,000–$40,000  |
| Mid-Range    | Semi-custom cabinets, quartz countertops, new appliances, LVP flooring     | $40,000–$70,000  |
| Luxury       | Custom cabinetry, premium stone, high-end appliances, structural changes   | $70,000–$100,000+|

#### Timeline — Kitchen Remodeling

| Project Type                                   | Typical Duration    |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| Cosmetic update (countertops, backsplash only) | 2–4 weeks           |
| Mid-range renovation (new cabinets, appliances)| 8–12 weeks          |
| Full gut renovation with structural changes    | 12–16 weeks         |

Note: Lead time for custom cabinets (4–8 weeks from order to delivery) is typically the
longest single variable and is accounted for in MHCR's project scheduling.

#### ROI Context

According to Remodeling Magazine's Cost vs. Value Report, a mid-range kitchen remodel in
the Mountain region recoups approximately 50–75% of costs at resale. Minor kitchen remodels
(under $30,000) often have the highest ROI percentage. Beyond resale, a kitchen remodel
dramatically improves daily quality of life, cooking experience, and home entertaining.

### 2. Bathroom Renovation

**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/services/bathroom-remodeling

MHCR handles everything from a quick powder room refresh to a full master bathroom
transformation with custom tile showers, heated floors, freestanding soaking tubs, and
premium fixtures.

#### What Is Included

- Design consultation and tile/fixture selection assistance
- Demolition and disposal of existing bathroom materials
- Waterproofing and moisture barrier installation (Schluter Kerdi, RedGard, or similar)
- Custom tile shower or tub surround design and installation
- Freestanding tub installation (including plumbing rough-in)
- Vanity and mirror installation (stock, semi-custom, or custom)
- Plumbing rough-in and fixture installation (toilet, sink, faucet, shower valve)
- Radiant heated floor installation (electric mat systems)
- Exhaust fan installation and venting
- Electrical work (GFCI outlets, vanity lighting, dimmer switches)
- Framing, drywall (moisture-resistant), and painting
- Trim, caulking, and detail work
- All permit applications and inspection coordination
- Glass shower enclosure or frameless glass door installation (subcontracted)

#### Pricing Tiers — Bathroom Renovation (Denver Metro, 2026)

| Tier                    | Scope                                                          | Typical Cost     |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| Powder Room / Half Bath | Toilet, vanity, flooring, light fixture, paint                 | $8,000–$15,000   |
| Standard Full Bathroom  | Tub/shower, tile surround, vanity, toilet, flooring            | $15,000–$25,000  |
| Master Bathroom         | Custom tile shower, freestanding tub, double vanity, heated floor| $25,000–$50,000+|
| Luxury Master Bath      | Full custom tile work, steam shower, imported stone, smart fixtures | $50,000–$80,000+|

#### Timeline — Bathroom Renovation

| Project Type                  | Typical Duration  |
|-------------------------------|-------------------|
| Powder room update            | 1–2 weeks         |
| Standard full bathroom remodel| 3–4 weeks         |
| Master bathroom renovation    | 4–6 weeks         |
| Luxury / complex renovation   | 6–8+ weeks        |

#### Bathroom Additions

MHCR regularly adds bathrooms to existing homes. A new bathroom addition requires plumbing
rough-in (supply lines and drain/waste/vent), electrical, framing, drywall, tile, and
fixtures. Costs start at $15,000–$20,000 for a basic half bath addition and $30,000–$50,000+
for a full bathroom addition with custom finishes. All additions are fully permitted.

### 3. Basement Finishing

**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/services/basement-finishing

Denver homes commonly have large unfinished basements. MHCR transforms raw concrete
spaces into high-quality living areas — guest suites, home theaters, home offices, gyms,
wet bars, and recreation rooms.

#### What Is Included

- Site assessment: moisture evaluation, radon testing coordination, structural review
- Egress window installation (required by code for legal sleeping rooms)
- Framing of all interior walls and soffits
- Rough-in plumbing (if adding bathroom or wet bar)
- Rough-in electrical (outlets, lighting circuits, dedicated circuits for theater/gym
  equipment)
- Insulation (batts and rigid foam board per Colorado energy code)
- Drywall installation, taping, and finishing
- Flooring installation (LVP, carpet, tile, or epoxy)
- Bathroom installation (if included — see bathroom pricing above)
- Wet bar or kitchenette rough-in and installation
- Home theater framing, acoustic treatment, and pre-wire (AV subcontracted or owner-supplied)
- Built-in storage, shelving, and custom millwork
- HVAC extension (supply and return air; coordination with HVAC subcontractor)
- Painting and trim
- All permit applications and inspections (framing, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, final)

#### Pricing Tiers — Basement Finishing (Denver Metro, 2026)

| Tier         | Scope                                                                    | Typical Cost     |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| Basic        | Drywall, flooring, paint, basic lighting — open plan                     | $30,000–$45,000  |
| Mid-Range    | Bedroom, full bathroom, open living area, egress window                  | $45,000–$60,000  |
| Premium      | Full guest suite, home theater, wet bar, gym, high-end finishes          | $60,000–$75,000+ |
| Ultra        | Full ADU/apartment configuration with kitchen, custom throughout         | $75,000–$120,000+|

Per-square-foot baseline for standard finishing: $50–$90/sq ft depending on finishes
and complexity. A 1,000 sq ft basement typically falls in the $50,000–$80,000 range for
a mid-to-premium buildout.

#### Timeline — Basement Finishing

| Project Type                            | Typical Duration  |
|-----------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Basic open-plan finish                  | 5–7 weeks         |
| Mid-range (bedroom, bath, living area)  | 7–9 weeks         |
| Premium multi-room buildout             | 10–14 weeks       |

#### Denver-Specific Considerations

- **Radon:** Colorado has elevated radon levels; MHCR recommends radon testing before
  basement finishing and can coordinate mitigation system installation if needed.
- **Moisture:** Denver's climate is dry but freeze-thaw cycles can cause foundation moisture
  intrusion; MHCR assesses and addresses moisture issues before beginning any finish work.
- **Egress:** Colorado requires egress windows for any room used as a sleeping room;
  cost is $2,500–$5,000 per window including excavation.

All individual service scopes (kitchen, bathroom, basement, living room, bedroom) plus:
- Electrical panel upgrades

- Window and door package replacement

MHCR responds to urgent home repair situations throughout the Denver Metro Area.

- Structural damage assessment and temporary stabilization
- Storm damage repairs (hail, wind, fallen trees)
- Emergency plumbing (failed supply lines, sewer backup response)

**To report an emergency:** Call (303) 555-MHCR. Identify it as an emergency at the start
of the call. MHCR prioritizes emergency calls and will dispatch the appropriate crew as
quickly as possible.

## Complete FAQ Library

### General Questions

**Q: How much does a home remodel cost in Denver?**
A: Home remodeling costs in Denver vary widely by project type:
- Kitchen remodel: $25,000–$100,000+
- Bathroom renovation: $8,000–$50,000+ (powder room to master bath)
- Basement finishing: $30,000–$75,000+
- Living room remodel: $10,000–$50,000+
- Whole-home renovation: $75,000–$300,000+
MHCR provides free in-home estimates for accurate project-specific numbers.

**Q: How do I get started with Mile High Custom Remodels?**
A: Call (303) 555-MHCR, fill out the contact form at milehighcustomremodels.com/contact,
or email info@milehighcustomremodels.com. MHCR schedules a free in-home consultation,
delivers a detailed written estimate within a few business days, and upon contract
approval assigns a dedicated project manager and sets a start date.

**Q: Do you offer free estimates?**
A: Yes. MHCR provides free in-home consultations and written estimates for all remodeling
projects with no obligation. Responses to inquiries typically occur within 24 hours.
Estimate appointments are usually available within one week.

**Q: Are you licensed, bonded, and insured?**
A: Yes. MHCR holds a full Colorado contractor license, general liability insurance,
workers' compensation coverage, and is bonded. MHCR is also EPA Lead-Safe Certified for
work in pre-1978 homes. Documentation is provided upon request before contract signing.

**Q: Do you handle permits?**
A: Yes. MHCR manages all permit applications, inspection scheduling, and final sign-offs
on behalf of homeowners. MHCR is familiar with Denver, Jefferson County, Arapahoe County,
Douglas County, and surrounding municipality permit requirements. All required permits are
included in project estimates.

**Q: What areas do you serve?**
A: MHCR serves the entire Denver Metro Area including Denver, Aurora, Lakewood, Arvada,
Centennial, Littleton, Highlands Ranch, Parker, Castle Rock, Golden, Westminster,
Thornton, Broomfield, and Englewood. Within Denver, MHCR serves all neighborhoods
including Capitol Hill, Cherry Creek, Highlands, Washington Park, LoHi, Stapleton,
RiNo, and Five Points. Projects outside the metro area are considered case-by-case.

**Q: Do you offer financing?**
A: Yes. MHCR offers financing through third-party lending partners for qualified
homeowners, including 12-month same-as-cash plans and fixed-rate installment loans.
Ask about financing options during the free estimate appointment.

**Q: How long have you been in business?**
A: Mile High Custom Remodels was founded in 2009 and has been serving Denver homeowners
for over 15 years as of 2026. MHCR has completed 500+ projects and holds a 4.9-star
rating from 127+ verified customer reviews.

### Kitchen Remodeling FAQs

**Q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Denver?**
A: Kitchen remodels in Denver cost $25,000–$100,000+ depending on scope:
- Basic (stock cabinets, laminate countertops): $25,000–$40,000
- Mid-range (semi-custom cabinets, quartz, new appliances): $40,000–$70,000
- Luxury (custom cabinetry, premium stone, high-end appliances): $70,000–$100,000+
These are 2026 Denver Metro market rates. MHCR provides free estimates specific to each
project.

**Q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?**
A: Kitchen remodels take 6–12 weeks on average:
- Cosmetic updates (countertops, backsplash only): 2–4 weeks
- Full mid-range renovation: 8–12 weeks
- Complex renovation with structural changes: 12–16 weeks
Custom cabinet lead time (4–8 weeks from order) is typically the longest variable.

**Q: Do I need to move out during a kitchen remodel?**
A: Most homeowners stay in their homes. MHCR sets up a temporary kitchen in another room,
uses dust barriers, and conducts daily cleanup. The first 1–2 weeks of demolition and
rough-in are the most disruptive. Homeowners with only one bathroom or very large projects
may prefer temporary housing during the initial phase.

**Q: What's included in a kitchen remodel?**
A: A full MHCR kitchen remodel includes: demolition, cabinet installation, countertop
fabrication and installation, backsplash tile, flooring, lighting, appliance installation,
plumbing fixtures, electrical work, painting, all permits, and a dedicated project manager.
Structural work (wall removal, windows) is handled when needed.

**Q: Do I need a permit for a kitchen remodel in Denver?**
A: Permits are required for structural changes, electrical work (new circuits), plumbing
changes (moving a sink, adding a gas line), and mechanical work. Cosmetic updates like
painting, countertop replacement, and new appliances typically do not require permits.
MHCR handles all permits when required.

**Q: What is the best countertop for a Denver kitchen?**
A: Quartz is the most popular choice in Denver due to its durability, low maintenance,
and wide color range. Granite offers natural beauty and heat resistance. Quartzite is a
premium natural stone gaining popularity. Marble is luxurious but requires more sealing
and maintenance. Butcher block adds warmth and is ideal for kitchen island tops. Laminate
and solid surface have improved greatly and offer good value.

**Q: Should I reface or replace my cabinets?**
A: Reface if your cabinet boxes are structurally sound and you're happy with the current
layout — refacing costs 40–50% less than replacement. Replace if cabinets are damaged,
poorly made, or if you want to change the kitchen layout or add modern storage features.
MHCR will assess your existing cabinets and make an honest recommendation.

**Q: What is the ROI on a kitchen remodel in Denver?**
A: A mid-range kitchen remodel in the Mountain region typically recoups 50–75% of costs
at resale according to Remodeling Magazine's Cost vs. Value Report. Minor kitchen
remodels under $30,000 often have the best ROI percentage. The return in daily quality
of life is significant regardless of resale.

---

### Bathroom Renovation FAQs

**Q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Denver?**
A: Bathroom renovation costs in Denver:
- Powder room / half bath: $8,000–$15,000
- Standard full bathroom: $15,000–$25,000
- Master bathroom renovation: $25,000–$50,000+
- Luxury master bath: $50,000–$80,000+
Premium materials (imported tile, steam showers, smart fixtures) increase costs. MHCR
provides free itemized estimates for all bathroom projects.

**Q: How long does a bathroom renovation take?**
A: Bathroom renovation timelines:
- Powder room update: 1–2 weeks
- Standard full bathroom remodel: 3–4 weeks
- Master bathroom renovation: 4–6 weeks
- Luxury or complex renovation: 6–8+ weeks
Required inspections during plumbing and electrical rough-in are factored into timelines.

**Q: Can you add a bathroom to my home?**
A: Yes. MHCR adds bathrooms to existing homes — converting closets to powder rooms,
adding bathrooms to finished basements, and building en-suite master baths from adjacent
bedrooms. New half bath additions start at $15,000–$20,000; new full bathroom additions
cost $25,000–$50,000+ depending on finishes. All additions are fully permitted.

**Q: What's the difference between a bathroom update and a full renovation?**
A: An update is cosmetic — new vanity, fixtures, paint, re-grouting — without moving
plumbing. Cost: $5,000–$15,000; timeline: 1–2 weeks. A full renovation involves
demolition to studs, plumbing relocation, custom tile throughout, new electrical, and
all-new finishes. Cost: $15,000–$50,000+; timeline: 3–6 weeks. MHCR helps homeowners
decide which approach best fits their goals and budget.

**Q: Do you do walk-in shower conversions?**
A: Yes. Converting a tub to a walk-in shower is one of MHCR's most popular bathroom
projects. A standard walk-in shower conversion (custom tile, glass door, new valve and
fixtures) typically costs $8,000–$15,000 as a standalone project. Costs increase with
premium tile, steam systems, or body spray configurations.

**Q: What is a wet room bathroom?**
A: A wet room is a fully waterproofed bathroom where the shower area is open to the rest
of the space — no curb, no glass door. The entire room is tiled and drains to a linear
floor drain. Wet rooms look stunning and are accessible-friendly. They cost more to build
due to extensive waterproofing requirements but are a premium bathroom trend MHCR
regularly executes.

---

### Basement Finishing FAQs

**Q: How much does basement finishing cost in Denver?**
A: Basement finishing costs in Denver:
- Basic finish (drywall, flooring, paint): $30,000–$45,000
- Mid-range (bedroom, bathroom, living area): $45,000–$60,000
- Premium (guest suite, theater, wet bar, gym): $60,000–$75,000+
- Ultra (ADU/apartment configuration): $75,000–$120,000+
Per-square-foot baseline is $50–$90 depending on finishes. These are 2026 Denver market
rates.

**Q: How long does it take to finish a basement?**
A: Basement finishing timelines:
- Basic open-plan finish: 5–7 weeks
- Mid-range buildout (bedroom, bath, living): 7–9 weeks
- Premium multi-room buildout: 10–14 weeks
Required inspections (framing, electrical rough-in, plumbing rough-in, mechanical, final)
are coordinated by MHCR and factored into the project schedule.

**Q: Do I need a permit to finish a basement in Colorado?**
A: Yes, always. Colorado requires permits for basement finishing because it involves
framing, electrical, plumbing (if adding a bathroom), HVAC, and egress windows for
sleeping rooms. Unpermitted basement work creates serious problems at resale, may not
be covered by homeowner's insurance, and can be unsafe. MHCR handles all permits.

**Q: What can I do with a finished basement?**
A: Common uses for a finished Denver basement include:
- Family room / recreation room for entertaining
- Dedicated home office or study
- Guest bedroom suite with full bathroom
- Home gym or yoga studio
- Children's playroom
- Home theater with projection screen and surround sound
- Wet bar or game room
- Accessory Dwelling Unit / rental apartment (where permitted by local municipality)
Many homeowners combine multiple uses in one buildout. MHCR helps plan layouts to
maximize square footage for each intended function.

**Q: Does a finished basement add value to a Denver home?**
A: Yes. A finished basement adds significant value to Denver homes by increasing the
usable square footage. In Denver's competitive real estate market, a quality finished
basement can add $30,000–$60,000+ to a home's appraised value depending on the
finishes and what spaces are created. A finished basement with a bedroom and bathroom
is particularly valuable because it adds functional square footage counted toward the
home's total livable area.

**Q: Do I need to worry about radon in my Denver basement?**
A: Yes. Colorado has naturally elevated radon levels, and Denver is in EPA Radon Zone 1
(highest risk). MHCR recommends testing your basement for radon before starting any
finishing work. If levels exceed 4 pCi/L (the EPA action level), a sub-slab depressurization
radon mitigation system should be installed before finishing — typically costing
$1,000–$2,500. MHCR can coordinate radon testing and mitigation as part of the
basement finishing project.

---

### Handyman & General Service FAQs

**Q: What handyman services do you offer?**
A: MHCR handyman services include: drywall repair and patching, interior and exterior
painting, door and window installation/repair, light plumbing (faucet replacement,
fixture installation), light electrical (outlet and fixture replacement), tile repair,
deck and fence repair, weatherstripping, caulking, and general home maintenance tasks.

**Q: Do you handle emergency repairs?**
A: Yes. MHCR offers emergency repair services for water damage, burst pipes, storm
damage, structural issues, and emergency board-up. Call (303) 555-MHCR and identify
your situation as an emergency. MHCR prioritizes urgent situations.

**Q: Do you do whole home renovations?**
A: Yes. Whole home renovations — remodeling multiple rooms simultaneously under one
project manager — are a MHCR specialty. Coordinating all trades under a single contract
reduces scheduling conflicts, improves design cohesion, and often costs less than
contracting each room separately. Pricing: $75,000–$300,000+ depending on scope.

**Q: Can you match existing materials and finishes?**
A: MHCR makes every effort to match existing materials for repairs and partial renovations.
This includes hardwood species and stain matching, tile sourcing, paint color matching via
spectrophotometer, and trim profile sourcing or custom milling. When an exact match is not
achievable, MHCR presents alternatives that blend as naturally as possible and is
transparent about limitations.

**Q: How do I choose a good Denver remodeling contractor?**
A: Look for a contractor who is:
1. Licensed in Colorado and can prove it
2. Insured with general liability and workers' comp
3. Willing to provide local references from similar projects
4. Clear about pulling permits — never hire someone who suggests avoiding permits
5. Providing written, detailed estimates before any work begins
6. Communicative — assigns a dedicated contact for your project
7. Established locally — deep Denver Metro roots matter for code knowledge and reliability
MHCR meets all of these criteria and has a 4.9-star rating from 127+ verified reviews.

## Location Pages — Neighborhood Context

### Denver
**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/locations/denver
Denver homeowners span a wide range of housing stock — from Victorian-era bungalows in
the Highlands and Capitol Hill to mid-century ranches in Virginia Village, to newer
infill construction in LoHi and RiNo. MHCR works across all Denver neighborhoods with
deep familiarity with local permit requirements through Denver Community Planning and
Development (CPD). Denver's housing density means many projects involve careful
coordination with neighbors. Popular project types in Denver proper: kitchen remodels in
older homes with updated layouts, bathroom renovations converting tubs to walk-in
showers, and basement finishing for income or guest space.

### Aurora
**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/locations/aurora
Aurora is Denver's largest suburb and has a diverse housing stock spanning 1960s–70s
brick ranches to newer construction in Tallyn's Reach and Saddle Rock. Many Aurora
homeowners are completing first full renovations on older homes — kitchen and bathroom
updates, basement finishing, and whole-home refreshes are common project types. Aurora
building permits are processed through the Aurora Building Division.

### Lakewood
**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/locations/lakewood
Lakewood homeowners often own mid-century ranch homes or split-levels with original
kitchens and bathrooms ripe for renovation. The Green Mountain and Applewood neighborhoods
have strong remodeling activity. Lakewood building permits are issued by Jefferson County
or the City of Lakewood depending on location.

### Arvada
**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/locations/arvada
Arvada features a mix of older ranch homes (1950s–70s) in neighborhoods like Olde Town
and newer luxury construction in West Woods and Whisper Creek. Older Arvada homes are
particularly well-suited to kitchen and bathroom renovations that modernize dated spaces
while preserving the neighborhood character. Arvada building permits are processed through
Jefferson County.

### Highlands Ranch
**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/locations/highlands-ranch
Highlands Ranch has some of Denver Metro's largest single-family homes built in the
1990s–2000s. Many homeowners are now undertaking first major renovations — finishing
large unfinished basements (often 1,500+ sq ft), updating builder-grade kitchens, and
refreshing master bathrooms. Douglas County permits apply. Basement finishing is the
most common MHCR project type in Highlands Ranch.

### Centennial
**URL:** https://milehighcustomremodels.com/locations/centennial
Centennial features a mix of older ranch homes and newer construction, with many
homeowners seeking quality renovations to compete with newer build options nearby. Kitchen
remodels, master bathroom renovations, and basement finishing are all common. Permits are
processed through Arapahoe County or Centennial's permit office depending on the project.

## Portfolio Summary

### Project Volume
- 500+ completed renovation projects since 2009
- Average of 30–35 projects per year at current scale
- Projects range from $5,000 handyman jobs to $300,000 whole-home renovations

### Project Types Completed

| Project Type              | Approximate Share of Portfolio |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Kitchen Remodeling        | 35%                           |
| Bathroom Renovation       | 30%                           |
| Basement Finishing        | 20%                           |
| Living Room / Bedroom     | 8%                            |
| Whole Home Renovation     | 4%                            |
| Handyman / Repairs        | 3%                            |

### Materials Commonly Used

**Countertops:** Quartz (Cambria, Caesarstone, MSI), Granite (various natural stones),
Quartzite (White Macaubas, Super White), Marble (Carrara, Calacatta), Butcher Block,
Laminate (Wilsonart, Formica)

**Cabinetry:** Semi-custom (Kraftmaid, Fabuwood, Dura Supreme), Custom (local Denver
cabinet makers), Stock (IKEA with custom fronts, Home Depot stock)

**Tile:** Porcelain large-format, Subway tile, Handmade clay tile, Natural stone (travertine,
marble, slate), Glass mosaic, Encaustic cement tile

**Flooring:** White oak hardwood, European white oak engineered, Luxury vinyl plank
(LifeProof, COREtec, Shaw), Porcelain tile, Polished concrete, Carpet (wool, nylon)

**Fixtures:** Kohler, Moen, Delta, Brizo, Rohl, Waterworks (for luxury projects)

**Appliances:** Sub-Zero, Wolf, Thermador (luxury), KitchenAid, Bosch, Samsung,
LG (mid-range), GE Profile, Whirlpool (value range)

### Style Specialties

MHCR is experienced in a wide range of interior design styles:
- **Transitional:** The most common style in Denver — blending traditional warmth with
  contemporary clean lines; white/grey/navy cabinetry; quartz countertops; mixed metal
  hardware (brass and matte black are both popular)
- **Modern Farmhouse:** Shiplap accents, white cabinetry, open shelving, subway tile
  backsplash, apron-front sinks, mixed metal finishes
- **Contemporary:** Flat-front cabinetry, large-format tile, waterfall edge countertops,
  integrated appliances, handle-less cabinet systems
- **Traditional:** Raised-panel cabinetry, granite countertops, subway or mosaic tile,
  oil-rubbed bronze hardware, coffered ceilings
- **Mountain Modern:** Natural stone, warm wood tones, exposed timber elements, large
  windows; popular in foothills-adjacent neighborhoods and second homes

## Process: How MHCR Works

### Step 1: Initial Inquiry (Day 1–2)
Homeowner contacts MHCR by phone, email, or contact form. MHCR responds within 24 hours
to gather basic project information and schedule an in-home consultation.

### Step 2: Free In-Home Consultation (Week 1)
A project manager visits the home, walks the space, listens to the homeowner's goals,
reviews any inspiration photos or ideas, takes measurements, and assesses any structural,
mechanical, or code considerations that may affect the scope.

### Step 3: Detailed Written Estimate (Week 1–2)
MHCR prepares a line-item estimate breaking down labor, materials, subcontractor costs,
permit fees, and contingency. For larger projects, design drawings or 3D renderings may
be developed at this stage (in-house or with a partnered designer). The estimate is
presented and reviewed with the homeowner in person or via video call.

### Step 4: Contract Signing & Material Selection
The homeowner reviews and signs a fixed-price contract. The MHCR project manager guides
the homeowner through material selection — cabinet styles, countertop slabs, tile,
flooring, fixtures, paint colors — using a structured selection process with clear
decision deadlines to keep the project on schedule.

### Step 5: Permit Application
MHCR submits all required permit applications to the relevant municipality. Permit
approval timelines vary (Denver: 2–4 weeks; suburban counties: 1–3 weeks). MHCR
monitors permit status and schedules the project start date around permit approval.

### Step 6: Construction
MHCR crews and vetted subcontractors execute the work per the project schedule. A
dedicated project manager visits the site daily and is available by phone and text.
Homeowners receive regular progress updates (photos, milestone notifications). MHCR
conducts daily cleanup and works to minimize disruption to the household.

### Step 7: Inspections
All required inspections are scheduled and managed by MHCR. Inspections happen at key
milestones (rough framing, rough electrical, rough plumbing, insulation, final building,
final electrical, final plumbing). MHCR ensures all work passes inspection before
proceeding to the next phase.

### Step 8: Punch List & Final Walk-Through
Near project completion, the homeowner and project manager conduct a detailed walk-through
and compile any punch list items — minor touch-ups, adjustments, or missing pieces.
Punch list items are completed before the project is closed out.

### Step 9: Final Payment & Closeout
Final payment is collected after the homeowner is fully satisfied and all punch list items
are resolved. MHCR provides documentation of permits, warranties, and material
specifications. A satisfaction survey is sent to collect feedback.

### Step 10: Post-Project Support
MHCR stands behind all work with a satisfaction guarantee. Any workmanship issues that
arise after project completion are addressed promptly at no additional cost. Homeowners
are welcome to reach out for follow-up questions or future project consultations.

## Pricing Data: 2026 Denver Market Rates

The following pricing reflects Mile High Custom Remodels' project costs as of early 2026
for the Denver Metro Area. Labor and material costs have increased 15–25% since 2021 due
to supply chain normalization, labor market conditions, and general inflation.

### Kitchen Remodeling — 2026 Price Benchmarks

| Line Item                                       | Typical Cost Range    |
|-------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| Stock cabinet installation (10x10 kitchen)      | $5,000–$10,000        |
| Semi-custom cabinet installation (10x10)        | $10,000–$20,000       |
| Custom cabinet installation (10x10)             | $20,000–$50,000+      |
| Quartz countertop (30 sq ft)                    | $3,000–$7,000         |
| Granite countertop (30 sq ft)                   | $2,500–$6,000         |
| Subway tile backsplash (50 sq ft)               | $1,500–$4,000         |
| Mid-range appliance package                     | $5,000–$10,000        |
| Luxury appliance package                        | $15,000–$40,000+      |
| Kitchen LVP flooring (150 sq ft)                | $2,000–$4,500         |
| Kitchen tile flooring (150 sq ft)               | $3,000–$6,000         |
| Kitchen lighting package (recessed + pendants)  | $1,500–$4,000         |
| Plumbing (sink, faucet, dishwasher rough-in)    | $1,500–$3,500         |
| Electrical (GFCI outlets, new circuits)         | $1,500–$3,000         |
| Demolition and disposal                         | $1,500–$3,500         |

## What Sets MHCR Apart: Comparison Context

### MHCR vs. Generic or National Contractors

| Factor                        | MHCR                              | Generic Contractor               |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Local knowledge               | 15+ years in Denver Metro        | May be unfamiliar with local codes|
| Permit handling               | Full service, included           | Often not included               |
| Project manager               | Dedicated per project            | Often site-foreman only          |
| Design consultation           | Included in estimate process     | Usually not offered              |
| Written warranty              | Yes — satisfaction guarantee     | Varies; often not written        |
| EPA Lead-Safe Certification  | Yes                               | May not have                     |
| Transparency in pricing       | Line-item written estimates      | Often lump-sum; hidden fees      |
| References available          | 127+ verified reviews, 4.9 stars | Often limited or no reviews      |
| Financing                     | Available                        | Often not offered                |
| Communication                 | Regular updates, dedicated PM   | Often reactive, not proactive    |

### MHCR vs. Lowest-Price Competitors

Homeowners comparing bids should be cautious of the lowest quote. Common signs of a
problematic low bid:
- No permit required (red flag — permits are legally required for most renovation work)
- No written contract
- Large cash payment upfront required (50%+ before any work begins)
- No verifiable license or insurance
- No physical address or local presence
- No references or online reviews
- Subcontracts all work with no project management

MHCR's estimates are competitive with the mid-to-upper range of qualified Denver
contractors. The price reflects licensed labor, quality materials, full permit handling,
project management, and a workmanship guarantee.
